title: Demand-driven quarterly strategy playbook for Hosted API + Model Fleet
creator: Lena Thompson
description:
Problem statement:
Our Hosted API model lineup and rotation cadence need a tighter, demand-driven quarterly planning process that balances latency SLOs, per-token cost targets, and rollout safety for model swaps. Current ad-hoc decisions create uneven capacity hedging, surprise cost spikes, and manual canary windows that slow velocity.

Goal:
Deliver a repeatable Q2 playbook that: (1) defines commitment lanes (core low-latency, cost-optimized, experimental), (2) prescribes capacity hedges and canary windows per lane, (3) ties each lane to clear metrics (P95 latency, cost-per-token, model-quality regression delta), and (4) documents rollback and fallback policies that can be automated by Engineering.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In-scope: Hosted API model lineup decisions, per-lane rollout cadence, canary schedule template, telemetry/acceptance gates, cost hedging guidance, cross-team coordination checklist.
- Out-of-scope: Private deployment on-prem rollouts (handled separately by Private product PM), changes to runtime kernel selection (owned by infra).

Artifacts and references:
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Quarterly+Demand-Driven+Playbook+Q2+2026
- Working spreadsheet (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/hostedapi-q2-playbook
- Canary cadence RFC (Google Doc): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-canary-rfc
- Example rollout automation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1187
- Canary results dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/hostedapi/canary-results

Planning assumptions:
- Demand forecast is based on last 8 quarters and current enterprise committed capacity (forecast attached in Drive).
- Two supplier model variants will be kept per lane (e.g., M-Base and M-Base-quant) to enable fast fallback.
- Cost target: reduce per-token unit cost by 12% vs prior quarter through smarter lane routing + quantization recommendations.

Success metrics:
- 95th percentile request latency remains within SLO for core lane during rotation windows (P95 <= 220ms).
- No more than one customer-facing incident attributable to model rotation per quarter.
- Achieve >=10% reduction in average cost-per-token for the cost-optimized lane after rollout.
- Canary gating automation reduces manual intervention time by 60% for rollout events.
acceptance_criteria: A Q2 playbook document published to Confluence with clear step-by-step runbook for model lineup decisions and canary schedule
Per-lane telemetry dashboard templates and threshold-based gates created and linked from the playbook
An agreed set of commitment lanes and example model mappings (core, cost-optimized, experimental) approved by Eng and Design
A canary scheduling template and rollback checklist that Eng can automate into rollout pipelines
A cost-hedge recommendation table with quantization and batching guidelines for typical workloads
comments: 2026-02-22 - Kickoff: Cross-functional kickoff with Eng (Sofia Nguyen, Rahul Patel), Design (Maya Chen) and Infra (Jonas Becker). Agreed to use demand forecast from Finance; Eng asked for lane-level SLA guardrails. Action: PM to draft playbook skeleton and lane definitions.

2026-03-01 - Draft review: Shared initial draft in Confluence. ENG feedback (Sofia): prefer explicit fallback models and prefer canary windows aligned to low-traffic hours for EU region. DESIGN feedback (Maya): require documentation of UX changes for degraded responses. Action: incorporate fallback matrix and regional canary windows.

2026-03-04 - Trade-offs discussion: We evaluated conservative vs aggressive lineup strategies. Decision: adopt conservative core lane (narrow changes, <10% traffic shifts per rotation) and a bolder experimental lane for new model types with limited burst capacity. Rationale: avoid latency regressions for core customers while keeping innovation velocity.
2026-03-07 - Eng follow-up: ENG provided rough automation tasks estimate (6 points) to add gate checks in rollout pipelines and hook canary dashboards. Added ENG-1842 as dependency for metric hooks.

2026-03-09 - Stakeholder sign-off: Presented to GTM and Customer Success for impact assessment. CS raised one enterprise customer with strict latency SLA; added a customer-specific hedging note and a runway of reserved capacity under Dedicated for that account.

2026-03-10 - Playbook draft finalized for Planning review. Next steps: schedule automation spike (ENG) and coordinate with Observability to deploy dashboard templates to staging. Added follow-up tickets for canary automation, dashboard templates, and release notes.
Links to follow-ups: Canaries automation ticket ENG-20111 (internal), Dashboard template PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/442
